name: Cenariu Orders & Inventory
author: cenariu

sections.description:
Free internal order and inventory management for producers, shops and distributors. It works independently, without WooCommerce, a paid license or a trial period. Test your business workflow and keep a backup before using it with live records.

Optional separate company accounts require the separately installed Cenariu Orders & Inventory Hosting module (provider API 1.0) on a single WordPress site. Free works independently without that module in standalone mode. Activate the compatible module before using My company. A site administrator explicitly enables company mode from My company; updating the plugin alone does not enable it. The existing ledger and its authorized team stay in the first company without moving or duplicating their records. Each new company has its own ledger tables, settings, customers, suppliers, stock, orders, payments, documents, numbering and reports. A WordPress user belongs to one company and an owner can add existing site users as inventory managers, operators, intake staff or couriers. No company role grants WordPress administrator, editor or media permissions.

The account page uses [cenaorin_account] and is created when company hosting is enabled. It links to WordPress sign-in and, only when the site permits it, registration. Public registration is not enabled by the plugin. A newly registered user must create a company or be added to an existing team; registration alone grants no access to any ledger. Use Subscriber as the WordPress registration default role. Company creation interrupted during table installation can be resumed by the same owner. Revoking or changing a member’s role invalidates their previous company forms and import/restore previews.

Company hosting is a one-way opt-in in this interface. Keep a full site backup before enabling it. Company JSON exports cover only that company’s 23 ledger tables, not the site-wide account registry, WordPress users or other companies. A hosting operator must also back up the entire site. WordPress media files are public and its media library is shared: attaching product images is disabled in this mode. Existing public media URLs are not made private. The site’s timezone remains shared. Temporarily deactivate PRO before first enabling company mode. After enabling it, activate a compatible PRO release with explicit account API support (integration tested with PRO 0.28.0); keep older incompatible PRO releases inactive. Legacy extension hooks are not dispatched in company mode. Each new company initializes its own PRO data explicitly; historical data are not copied to new companies. Paid subscriptions, payment processing, private file storage, cross-company user transfers and multisite/network hosting are not included.

Choose a producer, retail or distributor activity profile without changing the stock policy. The front form uses two screens: select or deselect multiple products, then enter all quantities and order details and save directly. The customer name is required. The editable delivery date defaults to the current date in the site timezone; other contact and delivery details are optional. Product cards show the configured image, unit price and selection state, while active orders have clearly separated cards. Retail checkout remains available. Distributor partial deliveries and invoices are not yet available. Configure products, units, quantity steps and prices. Enter orders with multiple products without available stock. Reuse customers by ID. Receive stock, mark orders delivered and record full or partial payments. Choose stock consumption on delivery or only after both delivery and full payment. Each order keeps its original rule. Completed orders remain in history. Edit pending orders, record returns/cancellations and refunds, and record paid expenses.

Customer management includes paginated search, editable contact/company/address/notes, current receivables and linked order history. Orders preserve the customer name and contact details from creation. Launch a new order from a customer record, including customers beyond the 500-entry quick selector. Set or reschedule an undelivered order’s delivery date with an audit reason; filter orders due today, overdue, in the future or without a delivery date. Dates follow the site’s timezone. No notifications are sent automatically.

An order intake role can only take orders. An order operator can also mark them delivered or paid. Inventory management, corrections and partial payments require the inventory manager capability. All interface messages use WordPress translations; the direct-install package includes Romanian translations. The directory package relies on WordPress language packs when available. Stored product names, units and customer details are not translated automatically. No WooCommerce dependency, external services or automatic homepage replacement.

A Delivery only role sees a separate queue of pending deliveries: historical customer name, phone, delivery address, date, product names, units and quantities. Structured prices, totals, currency and payments are not queried or included in its HTML. It can mark delivery, with each order’s original stock policy; it cannot take orders, record payments, edit stock or access financial reports, documents or exports. The public order page displays this queue instead of intake for this role. The queue is paginated at 50 orders. Custom roles combining additional capabilities retain their separately granted access. Contact and product text are user-supplied; avoid storing financial or sensitive notes in delivery fields.

Order lists in administration support search, status/date filters and pagination (50 orders per page), with CSV export of the displayed page. Financial period reports use each payment/refund/expense event date and export summary totals. CSV downloads require inventory access and contain customer data; they are not invoices. The front active list supports customer/phone/order-number search and pending delivery, unpaid or stock-reconciliation filters. Filters are preserved across pages and status actions. It uses 50 orders per page, with a total count and Previous/Next navigation for all active orders. Stock movement history is paginated with product/date filters and complete period totals per product; movement CSV exports the displayed page, while totals CSV covers the full filtered period. Customer selectors retain their previous limits.

Administrator JSON exports include all COI ledger tables. Media files and WordPress accounts are excluded. Validated JSON backups up to 2 MiB can be restored atomically into an empty ledger only, with a matching site timezone and a fresh safety backup. Existing records are never replaced or merged. Source user and image references are cleared; historical audit payloads retain original references. Recovery of cancelled orders, PDF/XLSX reports and invoicing are not yet implemented. PRO is planned as a separate extension; it is not bundled. There are no fiscal device connectors. In completion mode delivered unpaid products remain in the recorded stock. A receipt on an existing order is preserved if stock is insufficient; the order remains active until stock completion is retried. Quick counter checkout is atomic and requires sufficient stock.

The Commercial documents tab creates numbered offers and proformas from active orders, with issuer details, separate customer billing profiles, optional due dates, immutable item/price/party snapshots and audited cancellation. Each document type and series maintains its own consecutive numbers. Changing to an existing series resumes its numbering; cancelled numbers are never reused. Documents do not change stock, order totals or payments. Browser printing/Save as PDF is supported; no tax breakdown or fiscal invoice is generated. The complete JSON backup now covers 23 tables, including documents, events and numbering. Previous 18-table backups are accepted with empty commercial registers.

The Supply tab records suppliers and multi-product receipt documents, with optional manual unit costs. Receipt data is retained as a snapshot and every stock movement links to its document. Cancellation retains the document and creates inverse movements only when estimated physical stock is sufficient. Receipts do not automatically record supplier payments or expenses; unit costs do not constitute stock valuation, tax calculations or profit reporting.

Source code

The readable JavaScript sources are assets/front.js and assets/media.js. Readable CSS is in assets/admin.css, assets/front.css and assets/print.css. These are the original files shipped and loaded directly; no minification, bundler or build step is used for these assets. PHP source is included in the plugin root and includes directory.

Optional hosting provider

Company accounts require Cenariu Orders & Inventory Hosting 0.1.0 or later with provider API 1.0. The base keeps the secure resolver and privacy bridge. A site that previously enabled companies must install and activate the compatible module; otherwise company access is paused, including for global administrators without company access. Existing records, membership, company identifiers, audit, privacy settings and the opt-in flag are retained. Restore the module to resume access; do not downgrade or clear the flag. Classic standalone inventory remains available without hosting when company mode was never enabled. No subscription billing or public registration is enabled by this extraction.
sections.installation:
1. Install on a test WordPress site using 64-bit PHP 8.1 or later and a MySQL/MariaDB database with InnoDB support.
  2. Activate per site. Network activation is unsupported.
  3. Open Orders & Inventory. Set currency and decimal places before adding products.
  4. Select the Producer / later delivery, Shop / counter sales or Distributor / companies activity profile, and the stock rule for new orders: on delivery, or after delivery and full payment. Existing orders keep their original rule.
  5. Add products. Select a standard unit or enter a custom unit, quantity step, price and optional minimum stock. Choose the product image in the same form; access to the WordPress media library is required.
  6. Record initial stock or receive stock through the Supply tab. A saved order does not reserve stock; the configured consumption rule checks availability later.
  7. Use the order intake page created by the plugin, or add [cenariu_orders] to a page and include that page in your menu. The homepage is not replaced. Operators must sign in and have order intake permissions.
  8. Assign the appropriate role to each operator deliberately. The Delivery only role has its own delivery queue and cannot record payments or access financial reports.
sections.faq:
How do I upgrade an existing inventory?

Back up the full WordPress database and files before replacing the plugin. If Plugins shows “Upgrade existing inventory data”, an administrator with inventory access must run that action. Inventory operations pause until it completes; WordPress administration stays available. The upgrade retains existing records and moves the plugin’s historical table, option and permission names to the cenaorin_ prefix. Reload existing inventory forms after completion.

An interrupted upgrade can be resumed from Plugins. Keep the current plugin installed and retain its upgrade marker; do not delete or rename database tables to force completion. A diagnostic code explains a refused operation. Ask the hosting administrator to check database table-lock and rename permissions when database_error appears. Inventory ledger tables require InnoDB; shared WordPress options/usermeta tables do not need conversion. This upgrade does not merge conflicting inventories.

Does an order reserve stock?

No. A new order can be created without stock. Stock is checked when its configured consumption rule becomes satisfied. Partial payments alone never consume stock.

What if payment is recorded but stock is insufficient?

For an existing order, the receipt is retained and the order remains active until stock completion succeeds. Receive the missing stock and retry stock completion; do not record the payment again. Immediate counter checkout requires sufficient stock and completes atomically.

Can I change the stock rule for existing orders?

Changing the setting affects new orders. Existing orders retain their original stock rule and historical product, unit and price details.

Are offers and proformas fiscal invoices?

No. They are internal commercial documents with separate series and historical snapshots. Browser printing or Save as PDF is supported. No fiscal invoicing, POS or cash-register connector is included.

Does uninstalling remove my records?

No. Business records, roles and capabilities are retained. JSON backups exclude media files and WordPress accounts; restoration is supported only into an empty ledger, with a matching timezone and a fresh safety backup. It does not merge or replace existing records.

Does activation modify my homepage or the Catina plugin?

No. This plugin uses its own tables and an administration screen.

What customer information is stored?

Customer names, optional phones, addresses, company references and notes, orders and payment records are stored in the site’s database. Select an existing customer by ID or create a separate new record. User IDs and timestamps identify the recorded operations. This release sends no data to external services. Site administrators are responsible for access and retention. Data, roles and capabilities are retained on deactivation and uninstall. Commercial profiles may include email, tax/registration identifiers, bank and IBAN details; documents and audits keep historical copies. Import/restore previews expire after 15 minutes; expiration is not immediate physical deletion. Downloaded CSV/JSON/printable copies require separate protection. Suggested text is available in the WordPress Privacy Policy Guide; adapt it before publication. Site administrators in single-company mode, or company owners in separate-company mode, can export the selected customer record and linked business records as JSON after verifying the requester. Issuer profiles, operator IDs and operation tokens are excluded. Review free-text notes before sharing. This is not a restorable backup. These authorized owners may clear current phone, address, company, reference and notes after reviewed confirmation, only when no incomplete orders remain. Name, billing details, orders, documents, audits and downloaded copies remain; this is not anonymization. There is no automatic personal data eraser for commercial records. Commercial customers are not matched automatically by email. WordPress account privacy integration is described below.

What privacy tools are provided for company hosting?

Only the company owner can use Data privacy. Register verified customer requests for access, rectification, erasure or restriction, with append-only decisions and protection against stale forms or duplicate submissions. The register does not perform the requested measure automatically or send notifications. Personal exports and partial current-contact removal are available without WordPress administrator privileges; ordinary managers and operators do not receive these owner tools. Requests are selected by customer ID within the current company, not matched automatically by email. Review notes before sharing an export.

Customer request events are included in customer_changes in the existing 23-table JSON backup. Each company can record its contact and retention-review notes. A site administrator can configure the public hosting operator contact and an existing HTTPS privacy-policy URL, shown on the account page. These administrative options and company closure timestamps are outside the ledger JSON and require a full site backup. A closure request is recorded locally, keeps access active and must also be sent to the hosting operator using the provided contact link; the plugin sends no email. There is no automatic company purge, legal retention period or document anonymization. Complete the policy, processing agreements, retention and incident procedures before opening public registration. These tools do not certify GDPR compliance.

Are registered application users covered by WordPress privacy tools?

The WordPress personal-data exporter includes the current membership and related account-registry audit for an existing WordPress user matched by the request email. Callbacks require WordPress privacy-administrator permissions; a company owner cannot use them to inspect other site users. Audit results are paginated and omit other actors or subjects, operation tokens and business ledgers. WordPress handles its own request, nonce and delivery workflow; verify the requester before using it. Changed/deleted email identities and company business records require separate review. This is not a complete export of all data a company may hold about a person.

The WordPress eraser reports whether matching membership or registry audit is retained. It removes nothing and does not revoke access, delete a company or declare a legal retention obligation. The hosting administrator also has a bounded read-only company overview showing locally recorded closure timestamps, including companies without a request. The overview does not open their business ledgers or perform closure. Administrative privacy options and the site-wide registry remain outside the company ledger JSON backup.

Can each buyer configure their own application provider?

Yes. Go to Settings > Application provider. Any WordPress site administrator can configure the person or company offering the application on that installation, including an administrator who is not assigned to a company ledger. Enter the public name, email, optional address/identification and the published HTTPS privacy-policy URL. The policy URL can be left blank while preparing the service. Saving the public contact displays it on the account page; the plugin does not publish a policy automatically.

The provider profile is stored only in that WordPress site’s options. A new installation starts with empty fields and does not inherit Cenariu’s identity. Changing a company’s contact notes does not change the installation provider, and another installation has its own settings. Cenariu remains the plugin author. Provider settings and company administrative notes are not included in the company ledger JSON or the plugin ZIP; a full site backup/database clone may contain them. Review and replace them when cloning a site for another provider.

Does this generate invoices?

No. Invoicing is planned for a separate PRO extension.

A WordPress user belongs to one company and an owner can add existing site users as inventory managers, operators, intake staff or couriers. No company role grants WordPress administrator, editor or media permissions.

The account page uses [cenaorin_account] and is created when company hosting is enabled. It links to WordPress sign-in and, only when the site permits it, registration. Public registration is not enabled by the plugin. A newly registered user must create a company or be added to an existing team; registration alone grants no access to any ledger. Use Subscriber as the WordPress registration default role. Company creation interrupted during table installation can be resumed by the same owner. Revoking or changing a member’s role invalidates their previous company forms and import/restore previews.

Company hosting is a one-way opt-in in this interface. Keep a full site backup before enabling it. Company JSON exports cover only that company’s 23 ledger tables, not the site-wide account registry, WordPress users or other companies. A hosting operator must also back up the entire site. WordPress media files are public and its media library is shared: attaching product images is disabled in this mode. Existing public media URLs are not made private. The site’s timezone remains shared. Temporarily deactivate PRO before first enabling company mode. After enabling it, activate a compatible PRO release with explicit account API support (integration tested with PRO 0.28.0); keep older incompatible PRO releases inactive. Legacy extension hooks are not dispatched in company mode. Each new company initializes its own PRO data explicitly; historical data are not copied to new companies. Paid subscriptions, payment processing, private file storage, cross-company user transfers and multisite/network hosting are not included.

Choose a producer, retail or distributor activity profile without changing the stock policy. The front form uses two screens: select or deselect multiple products, then enter all quantities and order details and save directly. The customer name is required. The editable delivery date defaults to the current date in the site timezone; other contact and delivery details are optional. Product cards show the configured image, unit price and selection state, while active orders have clearly separated cards. Retail checkout remains available. Distributor partial deliveries and invoices are not yet available. Configure products, units, quantity steps and prices. Enter orders with multiple products without available stock. Reuse customers by ID. Receive stock, mark orders delivered and record full or partial payments. Choose stock consumption on delivery or only after both delivery and full payment. Each order keeps its original rule. Completed orders remain in history. Edit pending orders, record returns/cancellations and refunds, and record paid expenses.

Customer management includes paginated search, editable contact/company/address/notes, current receivables and linked order history. Orders preserve the customer name and contact details from creation. Launch a new order from a customer record, including customers beyond the 500-entry quick selector. Set or reschedule an undelivered order’s delivery date with an audit reason; filter orders due today, overdue, in the future or without a delivery date. Dates follow the site’s timezone. No notifications are sent automatically.

An order intake role can only take orders. An order operator can also mark them delivered or paid. Inventory management, corrections and partial payments require the inventory manager capability. All interface messages use WordPress translations; the direct-install package includes Romanian translations. The directory package relies on WordPress language packs when available. Stored product names, units and customer details are not translated automatically. No WooCommerce dependency, external services or automatic homepage replacement.

A Delivery only role sees a separate queue of pending deliveries: historical customer name, phone, delivery address, date, product names, units and quantities. Structured prices, totals, currency and payments are not queried or included in its HTML. It can mark delivery, with each order’s original stock policy; it cannot take orders, record payments, edit stock or access financial reports, documents or exports. The public order page displays this queue instead of intake for this role. The queue is paginated at 50 orders. Custom roles combining additional capabilities retain their separately granted access. Contact and product text are user-supplied; avoid storing financial or sensitive notes in delivery fields.

Order lists in administration support search, status/date filters and pagination (50 orders per page), with CSV export of the displayed page. Financial period reports use each payment/refund/expense event date and export summary totals. CSV downloads require inventory access and contain customer data; they are not invoices. The front active list supports customer/phone/order-number search and pending delivery, unpaid or stock-reconciliation filters. Filters are preserved across pages and status actions. It uses 50 orders per page, with a total count and Previous/Next navigation for all active orders. Stock movement history is paginated with product/date filters and complete period totals per product; movement CSV exports the displayed page, while totals CSV covers the full filtered period. Customer selectors retain their previous limits.

Administrator JSON exports include all COI ledger tables. Media files and WordPress accounts are excluded. Validated JSON backups up to 2 MiB can be restored atomically into an empty ledger only, with a matching site timezone and a fresh safety backup. Existing records are never replaced or merged. Source user and image references are cleared; historical audit payloads retain original references. Recovery of cancelled orders, PDF/XLSX reports and invoicing are not yet implemented. PRO is planned as a separate extension; it is not bundled. There are no fiscal device connectors. In completion mode delivered unpaid products remain in the recorded stock. A receipt on an existing order is preserved if stock is insufficient; the order remains active until stock completion is retried. Quick counter checkout is atomic and requires sufficient stock.

The Commercial documents tab creates numbered offers and proformas from active orders, with issuer details, separate customer billing profiles, optional due dates, immutable item/price/party snapshots and audited cancellation. Each document type and series maintains its own consecutive numbers. Changing to an existing series resumes its numbering; cancelled numbers are never reused. Documents do not change stock, order totals or payments. Browser printing/Save as PDF is supported; no tax breakdown or fiscal invoice is generated. The complete JSON backup now covers 23 tables, including documents, events and numbering. Previous 18-table backups are accepted with empty commercial registers.

The Supply tab records suppliers and multi-product receipt documents, with optional manual unit costs. Receipt data is retained as a snapshot and every stock movement links to its document. Cancellation retains the document and creates inverse movements only when estimated physical stock is sufficient. Receipts do not automatically record supplier payments or expenses; unit costs do not constitute stock valuation, tax calculations or profit reporting.

Source code

The readable JavaScript sources are assets/front.js and assets/media.js. Readable CSS is in assets/admin.css, assets/front.css and assets/print.css. These are the original files shipped and loaded directly; no minification, bundler or build step is used for these assets. PHP source is included in the plugin root and includes directory.

Optional hosting provider

Company accounts require Cenariu Orders & Inventory Hosting 0.1.0 or later with provider API 1.0. The base keeps the secure resolver and privacy bridge. A site that previously enabled companies must install and activate the compatible module; otherwise company access is paused, including for global administrators without company access. Existing records, membership, company identifiers, audit, privacy settings and the opt-in flag are retained. Restore the module to resume access; do not downgrade or clear the flag. Classic standalone inventory remains available without hosting when company mode was never enabled. No subscription billing or public registration is enabled by this extraction.
